prompt: An external partner needs to collaborate on a project by accessing some of your organization's SharePoint apps, but must not have a mailbox or an internal license. What is the correct approach in Microsoft Entra ID?

options.text: Create an internal member account with a Microsoft 365 license
Invite the user as a B2B external identity (guest user)
Share the credentials of an existing service account
Create a security group and add the partner's email address to it

explanation:
B2B collaboration lets you invite external users as guests using their home identities (the partner authenticates against their own IdP). The guest receives a user object in the tenant with userType Guest and can be granted access to resources without consuming internal licenses or requiring a mailbox.

Why the other options are wrong:
- Create an internal member account with a Microsoft 365 license: An internal member account with a license is wasteful for an external collaborator and creates a separate identity to manage, contrary to the B2B model.
- Share the credentials of an existing service account: Sharing service account credentials violates identity and accountability principles and is never an acceptable practice.
- Create a security group and add the partner's email address to it: Adding an email to a group creates neither an identity nor authenticated access: a real guest user object is required.

prompt: You want to enforce multi-factor authentication for all administrators when they access the Azure portal, regardless of their location. Which Microsoft Entra ID tool do you use?

options.text: A Conditional Access policy assigned to directory roles with a grant control that requires MFA
An Access Review on administrative roles
A Password Protection policy with a banned password list
An Entitlement Management access package with approval

explanation:
Conditional Access is Entra ID's if-then policy engine: it evaluates signals (user/role, target app, location, risk, device) and applies controls such as requiring MFA. By assigning the policy to administrative directory roles with the 'Microsoft Azure Management' cloud app and a 'require MFA' grant, you achieve exactly the desired behavior.

Why the other options are wrong:
- An Access Review on administrative roles: An Access Review periodically recertifies who has access, but does not enforce authentication controls at sign-in time.
- A Password Protection policy with a banned password list: Password Protection blocks weak or banned passwords but has nothing to do with enforcing MFA on access.
- An Entitlement Management access package with approval: Entitlement Management manages access package assignment through requests and approvals, not sign-in conditions.

prompt: Your organization wants administrators not to hold the Global Administrator role permanently, but to be able to activate it only when needed, for a limited period and with justification. Which feature do you implement?

options.text: Permanent active assignment of the role through role-assignable groups
Privileged Identity Management (PIM) with eligible assignment and just-in-time activation
Conditional Access that blocks the role outside working hours
Monthly Access Review of the Global Administrator role

explanation:
Privileged Identity Management provides just-in-time privileged access: the administrator receives an eligible assignment and must activate the role on demand, for a limited duration, often with MFA, justification, and possible approval. This reduces the attack surface by eliminating standing access.

Why the other options are wrong:
- Permanent active assignment of the role through role-assignable groups: A permanent active assignment keeps exactly the always-on privileges that you want to eliminate.
- Conditional Access that blocks the role outside working hours: Conditional Access can add controls on activation but by itself does not provide the eligible/just-in-time role model.
- Monthly Access Review of the Global Administrator role: An Access Review periodically recertifies assignments but does not enable temporary on-demand activation of the role.

prompt: Users frequently call the help desk to reset their forgotten password. Which Microsoft Entra ID feature reduces this load by letting users reset it themselves?

options.text: Password Protection
Self-Service Password Reset (SSPR)
Pass-through Authentication
Conditional Access

explanation:
Self-Service Password Reset (SSPR) lets users reset or unlock their own password after verifying their identity via registered authentication methods (e.g. Authenticator app, phone, email, security questions), reducing help desk calls.

Why the other options are wrong:
- Password Protection: Password Protection prevents the use of weak or banned-list passwords, but does not let the user reset them by themselves.
- Pass-through Authentication: Pass-through Authentication validates passwords against on-premises Active Directory; it does not handle self-service reset.
- Conditional Access: Conditional Access applies signal-based access controls, not password resets.

prompt: You need to configure Single Sign-On for a third-party SaaS application that supports the SAML 2.0 protocol, adding it from the Entra ID enterprise apps gallery. What do you configure on the Entra ID side?

options.text: An app registration with only a client secret for the client credentials flow
SAML-based SSO, providing the app with the Identifier (Entity ID), the Reply URL (ACS), and the claims/attributes
An Application Proxy private network connector with no other configuration
A Password Protection rule specific to the application

explanation:
For a SaaS enterprise app that supports SAML, in Entra ID you configure SAML SSO by setting the app's Identifier (Entity ID) and Reply URL (Assertion Consumer Service), plus the claims/attributes included in the SAML token. Entra ID acts as the Identity Provider, issuing the SAML assertion to the application.

Why the other options are wrong:
- An app registration with only a client secret for the client credentials flow: The client credentials flow with only a secret is for service-to-service (daemon) authentication, not for interactive SAML SSO of a SaaS app.
- An Application Proxy private network connector with no other configuration: Application Proxy is for publishing on-premises apps; it is not the SSO mechanism for a cloud SaaS that speaks SAML.
- A Password Protection rule specific to the application: Password Protection has no role in configuring an application's SSO.

prompt: The auditor requires that, every three months, managers confirm whether the members of certain groups with access to sensitive data should still retain it. Which Identity Governance feature do you use?

options.text: Access Reviews to periodically recertify memberships
PIM for just-in-time activation of groups
Password Protection on the groups involved
Conditional Access that blocks access to the groups

explanation:
Access Reviews let you periodically recertify access and memberships: designated reviewers (e.g. managers or the users themselves) approve or remove access at defined intervals, with the option to apply the results automatically. It is the governance control designed for cyclical recertification.

Why the other options are wrong:
- PIM for just-in-time activation of groups: PIM enables temporary activation of privileged roles/groups, not periodic recertification of memberships by managers.
- Password Protection on the groups involved: Password Protection concerns password quality, not access review.
- Conditional Access that blocks access to the groups: Conditional Access controls sign-in conditions; it does not run periodic membership recertification campaigns.

prompt: You want to prevent users from choosing passwords containing the company name and its predictable variants (e.g. Company123, C0mpany!). Which feature do you configure in Microsoft Entra ID?

options.text: Smart lockout with a low threshold
Password Protection with a custom banned password list
Self-Service Password Reset with security questions
Conditional Access based on user risk

explanation:
Entra ID Password Protection includes a global banned password list and lets administrators add a custom banned password list with organization-specific terms (company name, products, etc.). The system also evaluates fuzzy variants and common substitutions, blocking weak passwords at change time.

Why the other options are wrong:
- Smart lockout with a low threshold: Smart lockout protects against brute force by temporarily blocking after too many failed attempts, but does not prevent the choice of banned words.
- Self-Service Password Reset with security questions: SSPR allows self-service reset but does not enforce which terms are banned in the password.
- Conditional Access based on user risk: Risk-based Conditional Access acts on sign-in, not on the composition of the chosen passwords.

prompt: In a tenant you want to prevent users from granting consent to any third-party application that requests access to their data, and instead route the requests to an administrator approval flow. What do you configure?

options.text: Completely disable app registrations in the tenant
Configure the user consent settings to restrict/deny user consent and enable the admin consent workflow
Assign the Application Administrator role to all users
Create an Access Review on all enterprise apps

explanation:
The consent settings (Enterprise applications > Consent and permissions) let you restrict or deny user consent to apps, reducing the risk of illicit consent grants. By enabling the admin consent workflow, users' requests are forwarded to designated reviewers who approve or reject consent at the tenant level.

Why the other options are wrong:
- Completely disable app registrations in the tenant: Disabling all app registrations would prevent legitimate developers from registering apps and is not the targeted control over user consent.
- Assign the Application Administrator role to all users: Assigning Application Administrator to everyone would drastically increase privileges and risk, exactly the opposite of the goal.
- Create an Access Review on all enterprise apps: An Access Review recertifies existing access but does not intercept or route consent requests at the moment they occur.

prompt: You want to promote the most secure, phishing-resistant authentication method for your users in Microsoft Entra ID. Which method do you choose?

options.text: SMS as a second factor
Voice call with confirmation
FIDO2 security keys / passkeys (phishing-resistant passwordless authentication)
Security questions

explanation:
FIDO2 security keys and passkeys provide phishing-resistant passwordless authentication: the cryptographic credential is bound to the app's domain and cannot be intercepted or reused by fraudulent sites. Microsoft classifies it among the strongest methods, superior to SMS/voice, which are vulnerable to interception and SIM swap.

Why the other options are wrong:
- SMS as a second factor: SMS is a weak MFA method, vulnerable to SIM swapping and interception, and is not recommended as a strong method.
- Voice call with confirmation: The voice call shares the same weaknesses as SMS and is not phishing-resistant.
- Security questions: Security questions are a weak method, used only for SSPR and easily guessable or subject to social engineering.

prompt: You need to let employees request, on their own, an access package that bundles groups, apps, and SharePoint sites, with manager approval and automatic expiration after 90 days. Which Identity Governance feature do you use?

options.text: Entitlement Management with access packages and assignment policies
PIM for Groups without approval
Dynamic membership groups based on attributes
Conditional Access with a limited session

explanation:
Entitlement Management lets you create access packages that bundle resources (groups, apps, SharePoint sites) and define assignment policies with self-service request, an approval flow (e.g. manager), and automatic expiration/lifecycle. It is the feature designed for large-scale access lifecycle management, including for external users.

Why the other options are wrong:
- PIM for Groups without approval: PIM for Groups manages just-in-time activation of privileged memberships, not self-service assignment with approval of a heterogeneous resource bundle.
- Dynamic membership groups based on attributes: Dynamic groups assign membership based on attributes, without request, manual approval, or bundles of multiple resources.
- Conditional Access with a limited session: Conditional Access controls sign-in conditions and does not handle requests, approvals, or access package assignment.

prompt: Which of the following are valid signals (assignments) or controls you can configure in a Microsoft Entra ID Conditional Access policy? (Select 2)

options.text: The sign-in risk level as a condition
Automatic reset of the user's password
Requiring a compliant or Hybrid Entra joined device as a grant control
Rotation of the tenant's token signing keys

explanation:
Conditional Access evaluates signals such as sign-in risk (integrated with Identity Protection) and can enforce grant controls such as requiring a compliant or Hybrid Entra joined device, MFA, or approved apps. Risk and the device requirement are central elements of the Conditional Access if-then model.

Why the other options are wrong:
- Automatic reset of the user's password: Automatic password reset is not a Conditional Access control; resets are handled by SSPR or administrators.
- Rotation of the tenant's token signing keys: Token signing key rotation is a tenant platform/security operation, not an assignment or control configurable in a CA policy.

prompt: Which of the following are features or capabilities of Privileged Identity Management (PIM) in Microsoft Entra ID? (Select 2)

options.text: Requiring approval and MFA when activating an eligible role
Eligible assignments with time-limited just-in-time activation
Blocking banned passwords globally
Synchronizing password hashes from on-premises Active Directory

explanation:
PIM provides eligible assignments that the user activates just-in-time for a limited duration, and at activation it can require MFA, justification, and reviewer approval. It also includes notifications, auditing, and access reviews on privileged roles, reducing the risk of standing privileges.

Why the other options are wrong:
- Blocking banned passwords globally: Blocking banned passwords is a Password Protection function, not a PIM one.
- Synchronizing password hashes from on-premises Active Directory: Password hash synchronization is an Entra Connect (Password Hash Sync) function, unrelated to PIM.

prompt: Which of the following are authentication methods supported by Microsoft Entra ID that you can enable via the Authentication methods policy? (Select 2)

options.text: Microsoft Authenticator (push notification / passwordless)
FIDO2 security keys
The application web server's TLS certificate
The device's BitLocker encryption key

explanation:
Entra ID Authentication methods policies let you enable methods such as Microsoft Authenticator (push and passwordless), FIDO2 security keys, Windows Hello for Business, Temporary Access Pass, OATH tokens, SMS, and voice call. Authenticator and FIDO2 are valid and among the most recommended methods.

Why the other options are wrong:
- The application web server's TLS certificate: The web server's TLS certificate protects the app's HTTPS channel; it is not a user authentication method in Entra ID.
- The device's BitLocker encryption key: The BitLocker key protects data at rest on the device's disk and is not a user authentication method.

prompt: Conditional Access policies in Microsoft Entra ID are evaluated AFTER the first authentication factor has been successfully completed.

options.text: True
False

explanation: True. Conditional Access comes into play after the first-factor authentication (e.g. username and password) has completed: at that point it evaluates the signals (user, app, location, risk, device) and decides whether to grant access, block it, or enforce additional controls such as MFA. It therefore does not replace the first factor but acts as a subsequent decision engine.

prompt: An Access Review in Microsoft Entra ID is used to periodically recertify whether a user should continue to have a given access or membership.

options.text: True
False

explanation: True. Access Reviews allow you to periodically recertify access, group memberships, and app and role assignments. Designated reviewers (managers, the users themselves, or administrators) confirm or revoke access at defined intervals, and the results can be applied automatically, supporting compliance requirements and the principle of least privilege.

prompt: In Microsoft Entra ID an 'app registration' is the exact same thing as an 'enterprise application', with no conceptual difference.

options.text: True
False

explanation: False. The app registration defines the application and its identity in the home tenant (the Application object, with permissions, redirect URIs, secrets/certificates). The enterprise application is the service principal, i.e. the local instance/representation of the app in a tenant, on which you configure SSO, user assignment, consent, and provisioning. Registering an app creates the Application and, in the tenant, a corresponding service principal: they are distinct objects with different purposes.

prompt: In Microsoft Entra ID you want users from the Sales department to be automatically added to and removed from a group based on the value of the 'department' attribute. Which type of group must you create?

options.text: A security group with assigned membership
A security group with dynamic membership (dynamic user)
A Microsoft 365 group with assigned membership
An administrative unit

explanation:
Dynamic groups use membership rules based on user attributes (e.g. department eq 'Sales'): Entra ID evaluates the rule and automatically adds or removes members when attributes change. It requires at least an Entra ID P1 license.

Why the other options are wrong:
- A security group with assigned membership: Assigned membership requires manually adding and removing members; it does not update based on attributes.
- A Microsoft 365 group with assigned membership: A M365 group can also be dynamic, but here 'assigned' is specified, so it stays manual.
- An administrative unit: Administrative units scope administrative permissions; they do not manage automatic group membership.

prompt: An external vendor must collaborate on a project for 90 days. You want to invite them as a guest user and ensure their access is automatically revoked at expiration, without manual intervention. Which Entra ID feature is most suitable?

options.text: One-time access review on guests
Entitlement management with an expiring access package
Conditional Access with a block for guest users
Self-service password reset (SSPR)

explanation:
Entitlement management lets you create access packages with policies that automatically invite external users, assign resources and set an assignment expiration: at the end, access (and even the guest account, if configured) is automatically removed.

Why the other options are wrong:
- One-time access review on guests: A one-time access review requires a reviewer to decide manually; it does not guarantee automatic revocation on the planned date.
- Conditional Access with a block for guest users: Conditional Access controls access conditions in real time but does not manage the lifecycle or the expiration of the guest account.
- Self-service password reset (SSPR): SSPR lets users reset their password; it plays no role in guest access expiration.

prompt: With Privileged Identity Management (PIM) you want activation of the Global Administrator role to require a manager's approval and be limited to 4 hours. Where do you configure these requirements?

options.text: In the Conditional Access policies applied to administrators
In the role settings in PIM for Global Administrator
In the properties of the administrators' security group
In the tenant's authentication methods

explanation:
In PIM each Entra role has 'role settings' where you define maximum activation duration, MFA requirement, justification, approval requirement and the approvers. This is where you set mandatory approval and the 4-hour window.

Why the other options are wrong:
- In the Conditional Access policies applied to administrators: Conditional Access can require MFA at activation, but it does not define the approval workflow or the duration of the eligible activation.
- In the properties of the administrators' security group: Group properties do not control just-in-time role activation via PIM.
- In the tenant's authentication methods: Authentication methods establish how users authenticate, not the activation rules for privileged roles.

prompt: You want to allow access to Exchange Online from unmanaged devices only through a restricted browser session (no file downloads), blocking desktop clients. Which Conditional Access control lets you apply these session restrictions?

options.text: Grant control 'Require compliant device'
Session control 'Use Conditional Access App Control' (integration with Defender for Cloud Apps)
Grant control 'Require multifactor authentication'
Session control 'Sign-in frequency'

explanation:
The session control 'Use Conditional Access App Control' routes the session through Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps, where real-time policies such as block download, read-only or monitoring are applied, ideal for unmanaged devices.

Why the other options are wrong:
- Grant control 'Require compliant device': 'Require compliant device' would block unmanaged devices entirely; it would not allow a limited read-only session.
- Grant control 'Require multifactor authentication': MFA verifies identity but does not impose restrictions on actions during the session, such as preventing downloads.
- Session control 'Sign-in frequency': 'Sign-in frequency' controls how often reauthentication occurs, not the actions allowed within the session.

prompt: The company wants to adopt phishing-resistant passwordless authentication for administrators. Which authentication method meets this requirement?

options.text: SMS as a second factor
FIDO2 security key
Security questions
Voice call to the phone

explanation:
FIDO2 security keys provide passwordless, phishing-resistant authentication because they use public-key cryptography bound to the domain and do not transmit reusable secrets like OTPs.

Why the other options are wrong:
- SMS as a second factor: SMS is vulnerable to phishing, SIM swapping and interception; it is not phishing-resistant.
- Security questions: Security questions are a weak knowledge factor, used for SSPR and not phishing-resistant.
- Voice call to the phone: A voice call can be intercepted or subject to social engineering and is not phishing-resistant.

prompt: You need to delegate to a regional help desk the management (password reset, user management) of only the users in the Milan branch, without giving them permissions over the entire tenant. Which Entra ID feature do you use?

options.text: Administrative unit with a scoped role
Dynamic group containing the Milan users
Conditional Access with a Milan named location
Access package dedicated to the Milan branch

explanation:
Administrative units (AUs) let you group users/groups and assign administrative roles scoped to that AU. By assigning the Password Administrator or User Administrator role scoped to the Milan AU, the help desk manages only those users.

Why the other options are wrong:
- Dynamic group containing the Milan users: A dynamic group collects the users but on its own does not delegate scoped administrative permissions.
- Conditional Access with a Milan named location: Named locations define network locations for Conditional Access; they do not delegate administration.
- Access package dedicated to the Milan branch: Access packages manage end-user resource access, not administrative delegation for the help desk.

prompt: A third-party SaaS application supports automatic user provisioning via the SCIM standard. In Entra ID, in which section of the enterprise application do you configure automatic account synchronization?

options.text: Single sign-on
Provisioning
Users and groups
Conditional Access

explanation:
The 'Provisioning' tab of the enterprise application configures automatic SCIM-based provisioning: you set Automatic mode, the SCIM tenant credentials/endpoint and the attribute mappings to create, update and disable accounts in the app.

Why the other options are wrong:
- Single sign-on: 'Single sign-on' configures federated authentication (SAML/OIDC), not account creation/update.
- Users and groups: 'Users and groups' assigns who can use the app, but does not define the SCIM provisioning engine or the mappings.
- Conditional Access: Conditional Access applies access policies; it does not manage the account lifecycle in the app.

prompt: Identity Protection has detected that some users' credentials appear in a data leak (leaked credentials). You want that, when the user risk is High, a secure password change is automatically enforced. What do you configure?

options.text: A sign-in risk policy that requires MFA
A user risk policy that requires a password change
A Password Protection policy with a custom list
An access review on at-risk users

explanation:
Leaked credentials are a user risk signal. A user risk policy (in Identity Protection or as part of Conditional Access) set to High risk can require a secure password change, which is possible only after completing MFA, remediating the risk.

Why the other options are wrong:
- A sign-in risk policy that requires MFA: The sign-in risk policy reacts to the risk of a single sign-in, not to the cumulative user risk derived from leaked credentials.
- A Password Protection policy with a custom list: Password Protection blocks weak/banned passwords when setting them, but does not react to a detected user risk.
- An access review on at-risk users: An access review periodically verifies access; it does not automatically force a password change in response to risk.

prompt: A legacy on-premises web application uses Windows Integrated Authentication and cannot be modified, but you want to publish it securely for remote users through Entra ID with pre-authentication. Which solution do you use?

options.text: Entra ID Application Proxy
SAML-based single sign-on
App registration with OIDC
Seamless SSO with pass-through authentication

explanation:
Entra ID Application Proxy publishes on-premises web applications externally through a connector, applying Entra ID pre-authentication (and therefore Conditional Access/MFA) and supporting Kerberos Constrained Delegation for SSO to apps that use Windows Integrated Authentication.

Why the other options are wrong:
- SAML-based single sign-on: SAML SSO requires the app to support SAML; a legacy app with Windows Integrated Auth that cannot be modified does not support it.
- App registration with OIDC: OIDC requires modifying/registering the app as a modern client, impossible if the app cannot be changed.
- Seamless SSO with pass-through authentication: Seamless SSO is about transparent sign-in on the corporate network; it does not publish an on-premises app to the Internet.

prompt: You want to automate onboarding of new employees: two days before the hire date, generate a temporary password, send a welcome email and add the user to the correct groups, based on data coming from the HR system. Which Entra ID Governance feature do you use?

options.text: Entitlement management access packages
Lifecycle workflows
Dynamic groups
Access reviews

explanation:
Lifecycle workflows automate Joiner-Mover-Leaver scenarios: triggered by attributes like employeeHireDate, they run tasks (generate TAP/temporary password, send a welcome email, add to groups/teams) in time windows relative to the hire date.

Why the other options are wrong:
- Entitlement management access packages: Access packages manage requests and assignments of resource access, they do not orchestrate time-scheduled onboarding tasks based on HR dates.
- Dynamic groups: Dynamic groups update membership based on attributes, but do not send emails or generate temporary passwords.
- Access reviews: Access reviews periodically certify existing access; they do not handle onboarding.

prompt: A multi-tenant application requires an application-type Microsoft Graph permission (e.g. User.Read.All) that allows organization-wide access. Who must grant consent so that the app works for all users in the tenant?

options.text: Each individual user at first sign-in
An administrator with adequate privileges via admin consent
The application owner in the home tenant
No one: application permissions do not require consent

explanation:
Application-type permissions (access without a user, often broad in scope) always require admin consent granted by a suitable role (e.g. Privileged Role Administrator/Global Administrator). The consent applies to the entire tenant and cannot be granted by individual users.

Why the other options are wrong:
- Each individual user at first sign-in: Users can only consent to low-risk delegated permissions; never to application permissions.
- The application owner in the home tenant: The owner in the home tenant cannot grant consent in the customer tenant that consumes the app.
- No one: application permissions do not require consent: Application permissions always require administrative consent; they are not automatic.

prompt: Which TWO statements about Entra ID Self-Service Password Reset (SSPR) methods are correct?

options.text: Security questions can be used as a method for SSPR but are not allowed as a second factor for MFA
You can require users to register a minimum number of authentication methods to use SSPR
SSPR is not compatible with writing passwords back to on-premises Active Directory
SSPR and MFA can never share the same registration methods

explanation:
Security questions are allowed for SSPR but not for MFA. In addition, the administrator can configure the number of methods required for registration and for reset. With Password Writeback, SSPR also writes new passwords back to on-premises AD, and combined registration shares the methods between SSPR and MFA.

Why the other options are wrong:
- SSPR is not compatible with writing passwords back to on-premises Active Directory: False: with Password Writeback, SSPR can reset the passwords of synchronized accounts in on-premises Active Directory as well.
- SSPR and MFA can never share the same registration methods: False: with combined registration, SSPR and MFA share the same registered methods.

prompt: You are designing Conditional Access policies. Which TWO elements are considered 'assignments' (conditions) of a policy, and not 'access controls'?

options.text: Users or workload identities
Cloud apps or actions
Require multifactor authentication
Grant / Block access

explanation:
In a Conditional Access policy, assignments define to whom and to what it applies: users/groups/workload identities, cloud apps or actions, and conditions (risk, device, location). Access controls are instead the Grant/Block and Session controls applied when the policy triggers.

Why the other options are wrong:
- Require multifactor authentication: 'Require multifactor authentication' is a grant control (access control), not an assignment.
- Grant / Block access: 'Grant / Block access' is the policy's final decision, i.e. an access control, not a condition.

prompt: Which TWO statements about Privileged Identity Management (PIM) in Entra ID are correct?

options.text: PIM can manage just-in-time activation for both Entra ID roles and Azure resource roles
PIM can assign eligible membership to role-assignable groups (PIM for Groups)
PIM eliminates the need for Entra ID P2 licenses in the tenant
PIM prevents eligible users from activating any role without approval, in all cases

explanation:
PIM provides just-in-time access for Entra ID roles and Azure resource roles, and with PIM for Groups it manages eligible membership/ownership of groups (useful to bundle multiple roles or app access). It requires Entra ID P2 licenses.

Why the other options are wrong:
- PIM eliminates the need for Entra ID P2 licenses in the tenant: False: PIM is a feature that requires Entra ID P2; it does not eliminate the need for licenses.
- PIM prevents eligible users from activating any role without approval, in all cases: False: approval is configurable per role; not all roles require approval, it depends on the role settings.

prompt: In a B2B collaboration scenario with Entra ID, which TWO statements are correct regarding guest users?

options.text: A guest user authenticates in their own home tenant/identity provider and is represented as a guest object in the hosting tenant
External collaboration settings and Cross-tenant access settings control who can invite guests and which tenants are allowed
Guest users can never be assigned to Entra ID roles in the hosting tenant
Inviting a guest always requires creating a new password for them in the hosting tenant

explanation:
In B2B collaboration the guest authenticates at their own home identity provider and is represented by a guest object in the host tenant (userType Guest). External collaboration settings and Cross-tenant access settings govern invitations, allowed providers and trust on MFA/devices.

Why the other options are wrong:
- Guest users can never be assigned to Entra ID roles in the hosting tenant: False: guests can be granted Entra ID roles (although it is good practice to limit them); there is no absolute prohibition.
- Inviting a guest always requires creating a new password for them in the hosting tenant: False: the guest uses the credentials of their own home tenant; no password is created in the hosting tenant.

prompt: In Entra ID it is possible to configure an access review so that, if a reviewer does not respond by the deadline, the unreviewed users automatically lose access (removal).

options.text: True
False

explanation: True. In access reviews you can set the automatic action 'If reviewers don't respond': one of the options is 'Remove access', which automatically removes access for unreviewed users when the review expires.

prompt: Security defaults and Conditional Access policies can be enabled at the same time in the same Entra ID tenant.

options.text: True
False

explanation: False. Security defaults and Conditional Access are mutually exclusive: to use Conditional Access policies you must disable security defaults. They cannot be active at the same time in the same tenant.

prompt: In Microsoft Entra ID, the Continuous Access Evaluation (CAE) feature allows a session to be revoked or forced to reauthenticate almost immediately when critical events occur, such as the user being disabled or a password change, without waiting for the access token to expire.

options.text: True
False

explanation: True. Continuous Access Evaluation allows Entra ID and compatible resource providers (e.g. Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, Teams) to react almost in real time to critical events (disabled account, changed password, elevated risk, location change), invalidating the session without waiting for the typical token expiration (about 1 hour).
